videos.title: Self-Hosting Map Tiles: The Cost Breakthrough
videos.description: What if your map visualization never cost you money, no matter how popular it got? Commercial map services can become prohibitively expensive if your project goes viral [C3].
videos.transcript:
PMTiles, a tile format within the Protomaps ecosystem, ships in a single file and is accessible via Range requests, making it highly portable and easy to deploy.

PMTiles is a tile format that works via HTTP Range requests and can be deployed as a single file to a storage bucket.

In practical terms, storing the 139GB world map with replication to most continents (5x) will run you about $5/month in storage fees. At $0.05/1k map loads that could be 100x cheaper than Mapbox.

For example, you can extract data for only a bounding box or specific zoom levels, to get a significantly smaller file. With the tiles deployed, the only thing left to do is to embed them in your website via MapLibre GL, for example.

They support HTTP Range requests, don’t collect personal data by default, 2 are headquartered in the EU, and offer low-cost access to a global network of CDN and edge storage servers.

videos.title: Under the Hood: Jobs, Checkpoints, and Safe Publishing
videos.description: Dive deep into reliable automation patterns using checkpoints and safe publishing methods. We cover what it takes to build robust pipelines. AI-generated presenter and visuals.
videos.transcript:
A research claim only counts as verified when its supporting quote appears word for word in a stored source.

Jobs are stored in a database with checkpoints, allowing an interrupted render to resume without repeating the narration.

Duplicate uploads are prevented by a unique key for each channel, platform, and render, and the engine checks what the platform already has before any retry.

Publishing uses official platform APIs only, so YouTube uploads can be automated, while TikTok and Instagram fall back to a manual handoff package when automated posting is not approved. Emergency controls can pause publishing or stop every worker immediately.

Seven editorial workers write each script in turn, from research analyst to final editor, and every worker saves a new version instead of overwriting the last one.

videos.title: How Media Engine Keeps Every Video Honest
videos.description: When you build a studio entirely on your own hardware, the biggest threat isn't a crash—it's drift. The subtle, unmonitored slide away from the truth.
videos.transcript:
Media Engine is a fully local video production framework that runs entirely on a single Windows PC, requiring no cloud AI services at runtime.

A topic moves through a pipeline of discovery, scoring, a duplicate check, and research before anyone writes a script. A research claim only counts as verified when its supporting quote appears word for word in a stored source.

Seven editorial workers write each script in turn, with every worker saving a new version instead of overwriting the last. Jobs are stored in a database with checkpoints, allowing an interrupted render to resume without repeating the narration. Emergency controls can pause publishing or stop every worker immediately.

Every channel gets one permanent virtual presenter with a locked face and a locked voice, so the host looks and sounds the same in every video.

Videos are vertical, 1080 by 1920 pixels, assembled by FFmpeg with a presenter alternating with supporting graphics, plus captions and background music.

An independent quality stage must score each video at least 85 out of 100, and a hard failure such as an unsupported claim, a missing license or a missing AI disclosure blocks it regardless of score.

All language-model work goes through Ollama on the same computer, and the same graphics card also helps render the videos.
